Portrait de Dan, le Kickz Surgeon: Portrait of Dan, the Kickz Surgeon
Dan Desormes est né et a grandi dans l’u: Dan Desormes was born and raised in one of the poorest neighbourhoods in the country, Parc-Extension, and he still lives there today. For him, it isn’t just a place to sleep, but a place full of emotions that has watched him grow over the years. Today, Dan goes by the “Kickz Surgeon” (literally, the “sneaker surgeon”), which is also the name of the business he started. His trade, his passion? Cleaning and restoring shoes.
C’est par une fraîche soirée d’automne,: On a cool fall evening, at the Never Was Average studio, Dan sat down with La Converse. He chose the spot himself, and not by accident. “It’s a black-owned workspace that puts inclusivity and collaboration with the community first. I work here sometimes, and I feel comfortable and like I belong in this space,” he says as he settles onto one of the couches in the room.
Dan a jonglé entre sport et musique pend: Dan has juggled sports and music for much of his life. He first discovered his interest in music in elementary school. A student at école Barthélemy-Vimont, in the heart of Parc-Extension, he says it was thanks to his music teacher that he found his attachment to music. “In Grade 1, my music teacher talked to my mother. He told her I was good in his class, and he suggested she move me to a school specializing in music,” he says. After finishing elementary school, he continued on to a high school that also has a music focus. “I went to école secondaire Pierre-Laporte. Then, toward the end of high school, I drifted away from music a bit to focus on another passion of mine: football. So I enrolled at cégep Montmorency to join the football team,” he continues.
En pleine pandémie, durant les quelques: In the middle of the pandemic, during the few months when all of Quebec was in lockdown, Dan began looking for a way to fill his days. “Back then, I was a student athlete. We couldn’t play sports anymore because of the health measures. I had to find a way to keep busy while staying creative,” he begins. He pauses and starts to laugh, a little self-mockingly, then explains: “On Snapchat, in my private story, I asked people if they wanted me to clean their shoes. That’s how I passed the time: I’d put my music on in the background and work on my friends’ shoes. It was a way to relax while still being productive.”
Si le nettoyage et la remise à neuf de c: If cleaning and restoring shoes was just a way to kill time for Dan at first, the enthusiasm of those close to him for his work pushed him to keep going. “More and more people were coming to ask me to take care of their shoes. I realized there was demand, and that I could really do something with it,” he says. That’s why, in 2021, the young Montrealer officially launched his business. “I opened an Instagram page, found a way to promote myself a bit here and there, and here I am!” he says.
En tant que jeune d’origine haïtienne, i: As a young person of Haitian origin, he explains how his heritage and culture feed his motivation to do what he does. “When I saw how big the demand was, I was surprised at first. Then I realized that, actually, it was predictable. I’m an immigrant and I’m Black, and I know that in our communities, appearance is important. You’ve got nice shoes, nice jewellery, you pay attention to how you present yourself in front of others. In a way, I’m meeting a need. When people get their shoes back and see them all clean, good as new, they get the same feeling as when they just bought them at the store,” he sums up.
C’est aussi pour cela qu’il dit continue: That’s also why he says he keeps going and loves what he does: “When I look at people’s faces when they get their shoes back, I can see they really appreciate what I do.”
Dan a un frère plus jeune, et la fratrie: Dan has a younger brother, and the two were raised by a single mother. Watching his mother raise two children alone was, and still is, hard for him. “It leaves a mark on a child to see their only parent struggling for them. Paying the rent, buying groceries, making sure the kids are okay: it’s a huge task, especially when you’re doing it alone,” he recalls. The young man’s everyday life was thus shaped by a complicated family situation, but Dan is quick to point out that, despite everything, his mother managed to meet all her children’s needs: “Even though she was alone, my mother always took good care of us. But I know how hard it was for her.”
Un événement a fait basculer la vie de l: One event turned the little family’s life in Parc-Extension upside down. In the middle of the housing crisis, the boys’ mother received an eviction notice: they had to leave as soon as possible. “In 2018, the owners of the apartment we were renting told us to leave. We had to find an apartment very quickly, or we risked ending up on the street,” he says, still bewildered.
« Je me souviens encore de cette période: “I still remember that period. I walked for kilometres through the streets looking for apartments to rent in the area, because we couldn’t leave the neighbourhood. The change would have been too abrupt, and getting used to new places is demanding, even if it doesn’t look like it,” he says, to illustrate the mental load on his family. “I spent hours calling phone numbers, hoping the rents wouldn’t be too expensive, especially at the beginning of a housing crisis.”
« On devait partir le 1<sup>er</sup> jui: “We had to leave on July 1<sup>st</sup> that year. Two days before, we still had no place to live. Then, by a miracle, we found an apartment close to where we had been living. We were able to move, but it was close.” He stops mid-sentence to take a breath, as if the stress of that experience were coming back to him. “We were lucky, but I know others aren’t that lucky,” he continues, pensive.
<strong>Le changement du quartier qui l’: The changing neighbourhood that watched him grow up
Vivre une éviction, c’est une réalité de: Going through an eviction is an increasingly common reality in Montréal. Dan knows it, and he thinks that in Parc-Extension, it’s becoming more and more common, especially in the past few years.
Même s’il demeure très attaché à Parc-Ex: Even though he remains deeply attached to Parc-Extension, Dan doesn’t deny the change and transformation the neighbourhood has been going through in recent years. “I grew up and lived there all my life. I see the change, especially with gentrification. I’ve witnessed the neighbourhood’s evolution.” He then describes how, when they were younger, he and his friends went to the local parks to play. “I still remember the time I spent at Parc Liège playing basketball or soccer. Today, it’s not the same at all.”
Le jeune entrepreneur parle également d’: The young entrepreneur also speaks of a kind of exodus from the neighbourhood. “I see a lot of people leaving Parc-Ex. It’s sad, but I understand. The price of rent is ridiculous,” he says indignantly. “More and more students are coming to live here, especially since Université de Montréal built a campus nearby,” he says, referring to the construction of Université de Montréal’s MIL campus, located right near the Acadie metro station.
« Quinze ans plus tôt, tout ce que je vo: “Fifteen years ago, all I saw in the neighbourhood was a very diverse community. South Asians, Africans, Haitians: there were lots of diasporas here. Now people are leaving, and the ones who can afford higher rents are moving in.”
<strong>« Être pour les jeunes ce que je: “To be for young people what I never had the chance to have”
Dan poursuit présentement des études sup: Dan is currently pursuing postsecondary studies at Concordia University. “I’m studying to become an athletic director at the high school and college level,” he tells us. He reiterates that sports have always been a passion for him and that his goal is to give back through that passion by taking on a mentor role.
« Je veux redonner à travers le sport »,: “I want to give back through sports,” he repeats. Determined, he explains why becoming an athletic director matters so much to him. “I grew up with a single mother. I have a little brother too, and I saw how hard it is to be a single mother raising two boys,” he begins. He then looks up at the ceiling, as if thinking, and continues: “Through sports, my coaches encouraged me to stay in school and keep going. I kind of had father figures, because I saw successful men believe in me and push me to excel in school and keep at sports.”
Et c’est autant avec <em>Kickz Surgeon</: And it’s as much through Kickz Surgeon as through what he hopes to become later that he feels he can give back, in turn, to younger people. “I want to be for young people what I didn’t have the chance to have directly. I want to motivate them to stay on the straight and narrow,” he says.
Mais comment redonner ? Pour Dan, redonn: But how to give back? For Dan, giving back to the community is more than being a model of success, however accessible. “You have to go further. Me, I want to help and reach young people directly. I’d like, especially in my neighbourhood, to organize events and make sure young people have a positive view of their neighbourhood. I want there to be food, music, and people who’ve made it being accessible to these young people to motivate them,” he says, eyes shining.
L’intervention, pour Dan, ça passe aussi: For Dan, stepping in also means understanding young people. “I know I’ve been in the same place as a lot of young people in the neighbourhood, and I know I’m not the only one who’s been through hard things. I know young people think they’re destined for something, but I also know they need people who understand them rather than people who put them in categories.” Besides understanding young people, he believes they need to be shown that there are passions and ways out in life, “without staying outside, on the street, doing nothing and hanging around people who are a bad influence.”
« C’est un cycle », affirme Dan. « Il fa: “It’s a cycle,” says Dan. “We have to help the younger ones who think they have no hope. If we show them you can break out of this cycle, anything is possible,” concludes the Kickz Surgeon.
